ayurvedic_options.name: Aloe vera
ayurvedic_options.pros: A randomised placebo-controlled trial reported lower blood glucose and cholesterol.
ayurvedic_options.cons: One small trial only; the bitter latex is a harsh laxative; gel quality varies widely.
ayurvedic_options.cautions: Laxative latex can lower potassium; the gel adds to sugar-lowering medicines.
ayurvedic_options.source_note: PMID 22198821 (randomised double-blind placebo-controlled trial in type 2 diabetes)
ayurvedic_options.uses: Traditional use of ghritakumari gel for digestion, skin and metabolic complaints.

ayurvedic_options.name: Cinnamon
ayurvedic_options.pros: Common spice; a review of randomised trials reports modest falls in blood glucose.
ayurvedic_options.cons: Trial results conflict and the effect is small; cassia types carry a coumarin liver risk.
ayurvedic_options.cautions: Adds to sugar-lowering medicines; true cinnamon is preferred over cassia bark.
ayurvedic_options.uses: Traditional use of twak as a warming digestive and metabolic spice.

ayurvedic_options.name: Karela
ayurvedic_options.pros: Long traditional record for blood sugar; small human studies report lower glucose.
ayurvedic_options.cons: Human studies are small and mixed; very bitter; can upset the stomach.
ayurvedic_options.cautions: Adds to the sugar-lowering effect of diabetes medicines; watch for low-sugar symptoms.
ayurvedic_options.source_note: PMID 15521566 (human NIDDM study of hypoglycemic effect alongside oral antidiabetic drugs); PMID 19904502
ayurvedic_options.uses: Classical use of bitter gourd fruit for prameha, the sugar-related disease group.

ayurvedic_options.name: Amla
ayurvedic_options.pros: Common food fruit with a long rasayana record; animal work shows antihyperglycaemic effect.
ayurvedic_options.cons: Human evidence for blood sugar is thin; sour taste; can loosen stools.
ayurvedic_options.cautions: May add to sugar-lowering medicines; a human study shows added antiplatelet effect.
ayurvedic_options.source_note: PMID 21394805 and PMID 19761040 (glycaemic, animal); antiplatelet tag from PMID 24291054, a human study alongside clopidogrel and aspirin
ayurvedic_options.uses: Classical rasayana fruit, used in Triphala and recorded for prameha.

ayurvedic_options.name: Fenugreek
ayurvedic_options.pros: Widely used as food and medicine; animal studies show lower glucose and lipids.
ayurvedic_options.cons: Human trials are small; causes wind, loose stools and a maple-like body odour.
ayurvedic_options.cautions: Adds to sugar-lowering medicines; large amounts are avoided in pregnancy.
ayurvedic_options.uses: Traditional use of methi seed for prameha and for digestion.

ayurvedic_options.name: Garlic
ayurvedic_options.pros: Common food; animal studies report modest falls in blood glucose.
ayurvedic_options.cons: The effect on sugar is small and inconsistent in people; strong smell.
ayurvedic_options.cautions: Raises bleeding risk with blood thinners; a documented warfarin interaction exists.
ayurvedic_options.source_note: PMID 16801983 (glycaemic); warfarin interaction curator-confirmed in this project (PMID 10675182, 19719333, 21919844)
ayurvedic_options.uses: Classical use of lashuna as a warming herb for vata and circulatory complaints.

ayurvedic_options.name: Giloy
ayurvedic_options.pros: Long classical record; animal studies show lower glucose and better insulin sensitivity.
ayurvedic_options.cons: No good human trials for blood sugar; liver injury has been reported with some products.
ayurvedic_options.cautions: Reported liver injury cases; avoid alongside other medicines that stress the liver.
ayurvedic_options.source_note: PMID 1529024 and PMID 19520137 (glycaemic, animal); the hepatotoxic_risk tag rests on published Indian case series and is general knowledge, not on an abstract in this corpus
ayurvedic_options.uses: Classical rasayana, guduchi, recorded for prameha and for fevers.

ayurvedic_options.name: Gymnema
ayurvedic_options.pros: Strong traditional record; animal studies show lower glucose and better insulin response.
ayurvedic_options.cons: Human evidence is limited; may blunt sweet taste; product strength varies.
ayurvedic_options.cautions: Adds to sugar-lowering medicines, so low-sugar episodes are possible.
ayurvedic_options.uses: Classical use of gurmar leaf for prameha; the Hindi name means sugar destroyer.

ayurvedic_options.name: Moringa
ayurvedic_options.pros: Nutritious leaf eaten as a vegetable; animal studies show better glucose tolerance.
ayurvedic_options.cons: Human evidence is limited; large amounts can loosen the stools.
ayurvedic_options.cautions: May add to both sugar-lowering and blood-pressure-lowering medicines.
ayurvedic_options.source_note: PMID 26124050 and PMID 29175792 (glycaemic); blood-pressure tag from PMID 32412306
ayurvedic_options.uses: Traditional use of shigru leaf and pod as food and as a metabolic tonic.

ayurvedic_options.name: Neem
ayurvedic_options.pros: Long traditional use; animal work shows the leaf extract lowers blood glucose.
ayurvedic_options.cons: Human evidence is absent; very bitter; the seed oil is toxic, especially to children.
ayurvedic_options.cautions: Adds to sugar-lowering medicines; neem oil must never be given to infants or children.
ayurvedic_options.uses: Classical use of nimba as a bitter herb for prameha, skin disease and fevers.

ayurvedic_options.name: Turmeric
ayurvedic_options.pros: Everyday kitchen spice; animal and early human work suggests better glucose control.
ayurvedic_options.cons: Curcumin is poorly absorbed alone; evidence is early; can irritate the stomach.
ayurvedic_options.cautions: May slow breakdown of other medicines; a documented interaction with metformin exists.
ayurvedic_options.source_note: PMID 29518605 (curator-confirmed metformin interaction in this project); antiplatelet tag from PMID 16112857 and PMID 20158382
ayurvedic_options.uses: Classical use of haridra for prameha, inflammation and skin disorders.

allopathic_options.name: Glimepiride
allopathic_options.pros: Lowers blood sugar quickly and is inexpensive.
allopathic_options.cons: Real risk of low blood sugar, especially if meals are missed; can add weight.
allopathic_options.cautions: Not for type 1 diabetes; skipping meals can cause dangerous low blood sugar.
allopathic_options.uses: Prompting the pancreas to release more insulin in type 2 diabetes.
common_side_effects: rarely a drop in red blood cells

allopathic_options.name: Insulin
allopathic_options.pros: Works for anyone and can be adjusted precisely; essential when tablets are not enough.
allopathic_options.cons: Injections and monitoring are needed; low blood sugar is the main hazard.
allopathic_options.cautions: Must not be used during a low-sugar episode; never share a pen or needle.
allopathic_options.source_note: openFDA SPL label, set_id b60e8dd0-1d48-4dc9-87fd-e14675255e8c effective 20260701 (data/raw/openfda_labels.json)
allopathic_options.uses: Replacing or supplementing the body's own insulin to control blood sugar.

allopathic_options.name: Metformin
allopathic_options.pros: First-choice tablet; long safety record; does not usually cause low sugar on its own.
allopathic_options.cons: Stomach upset is common at first; cannot be used with poor kidney function.
allopathic_options.cautions: Carries a lactic acidosis warning; not used when kidney function is severely reduced.
allopathic_options.uses: Lowering blood sugar in type 2 diabetes, alongside diet and exercise.

allopathic_options.name: Pioglitazone
allopathic_options.pros: Improves insulin sensitivity and keeps working over a long period.
allopathic_options.cons: Causes fluid retention and weight gain; can worsen heart failure; raises fracture risk.
allopathic_options.cautions: Carries a heart failure warning and must not be started in moderate or severe heart failure.
allopathic_options.uses: Making the body's tissues respond better to its own insulin.

combination_warnings.label: Literature-verified
combination_warnings.reason: Curated PubMed evidence records general_interaction interaction language for Aloe vera and Insulin in 1 abstract(s) (PMID 28160765), each confirmed by manual curator review.

citations.evidence_sentence: The study found potential drug-herb interactions in 4 (50%) of the CAM consumers. Moderate potential interactions were found between Aloe vera and diuretics; Aloe vera and insulin; pyridoxine and calcium-channel blockers and diuretics; and niacin and statins. Those interactions had the potential to result in hypoglycemia, hyperglycemia, hypokalemia, and lower blood pressure.

citations.evidence_sentence: Herb-drug interaction of Nisha Amalaki and Curcuminoids with metformin in normal and diabetic condition: A disease system approach. Nisha Amalaki (NA), formulation with Curcuma longa Linn (Turmeric, Haridra, Nisha in Sanskrit; Family: Zingiberaceae) and Phyllanthus emblica Linn (Indian gooseberry, Amlaki in Sanskrit; Family: Phyllanthaceae) which is described for various diseases including diabetes in ayurvedic texts and Nighantus.

citations.evidence_sentence: Synergistic action of a Momordica charantia-abundant peptide with insulin regulates blood glucose metabolism in db/db mice via a novel second-hit mechanism on insulin receptor activation. Diabetes is a global health challenge, often managed with insulin therapy.
